subject: Production queueing + reserved throughput shortfall — exec convene requested
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prod queueing & reserved throughput delta (ClearStream) — urgent

Team,

We just received an alert from ClearStream (account DS-4721) that their production requests are seeing elevated queueing and intermittent 5xx spikes starting 02:00 UTC this morning. Initial telemetry indicates their reserved capacity is not delivering the baseline throughput they expect — we are seeing queue growth on their reserved pool and a rising 95th pct latency.

Quick facts from monitoring (prelim):
- Time window: 02:00–08:30 UTC
- ClearStream reserved pool id: rp-clar-3
- Avg QPS for their reserved routes: 220 (requested SLA baseline 300)
- Token throughput: ~70k t/s vs expected 95k t/s
- 5xx spike annotation: short bursts tied to queue depth > 600

Customer impact: delayed payment authorizations (they report transaction timeouts), operations is escalating to their execs. Grace, can you own the external comms? Marissa / Olga, can you pull the reserve metrics, kernel selection logs, and a snapshot of pool consumers (to check noisy neighbors)? We should convene an exec-level bridge for 15:00 PT today to align on mitigation and a temporary burst/credit path.

Attachments: I attached a quick snapshot I pulled from the dashboard (pool_usage_snapshot.csv) — Marissa, please replace/update with raw logs when available.

Goal for the bridge: (1) confirm root cause (kernel selection / oversubscription / customer token surge), (2) commit immediate mitigation (short-term slot reallocation or burst), (3) discuss credits and remediation timeline.

Jonas
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod queueing & reserved throughput delta (ClearStream) — urgent

Jonas — good catch. I pulled additional telemetry from the serving runtime and ops. Findings so far:

Diagnostics summary:
- We have sustained KV cache churn on rp-clar-3 caused by a new model variant the customer rolled last night (v2.4). The variant increases KV size by ~18% which exacerbates memory pressure and reduces effective batch sizes.
- Autoscaler attempted to add slots but hit the reserved pool ceiling (their committed capacity is pinned and there are concurrent workloads in the same pool).
- Kernel selection logs show a fallback to a less efficient attention kernel for long contexts on ~12% of requests (correlates with latency tail).
- Error pattern: most 5xx are OOM-related transient failures when cache eviction and batch consolidation collide.

Numbers (20-min sample at 08:00 UTC):
- Effective throughput per GPU: 6.2k tokens/s (expected 8.4k)
- Batch size distribution shifted down by ~22%
- 95th pct latency up from 220ms -> 820ms for their heavy routes

Attachments: pool_usage_snapshot.csv (updated), bottleneck_graph.png (visual) attached.

Immediate recommended mitigations:
1) Temporary re-route: shift non-critical ClearStream routes to a less-congested dedicated shard for 4–8 hours (requires ops approval).
2) Emergency burst: authorize a short-duration burst add of +20% capacity for the pool while we stabilize (needs exec approval because it overrides reserved commit).
3) Roll model revert assistance: offer a guided rollback to their prior model variant (v2.3) which removes the KV pressure (relatively low customer friction).
4) Longer term: offer a quantization profile or kernel tuning for v2.4 — R&D to scope (ETA 2–3 days).

Requesting: authorization for the emergency burst and an exec bridge at 15:00 PT (22:00 UTC) so we can confirm with the customer and do the re-route without surprise.

Marissa
Sr. Technical Ops Lead — Redwood Dedicated

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearstream.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: ClearStream: immediate support & exec bridge request (today 15:00 PT)

Alex,

Thanks for flagging this — I'm very sorry for the disruption. We're treating this with high priority. My name is Grace, I'm the lead for your account at Redwood. I've looped in our technical ops and customer success leads (Marissa and Jonas) and our infra lead (Olga).

What we know so far: there's queueing and latency on your reserved routes tied to the model variant you deployed. We have a proposed immediate mitigation (short-term re-route or emergency burst); Marissa is preparing a short diagnostics packet and a visual.

We'd like to get your team on an exec bridge today at 15:00 PT / 22:00 UTC so we can: (1) show the telemetry, (2) confirm the mitigation you prefer, and (3) provide a timeline for a rollback or patch. Can your ops or engineering leader join?

Please reply with who will be on the call and whether a temporary rollback to v2.3 is acceptable as a first step. We appreciate your patience; we'll make this right.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive — Midmarket Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearstream.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearStream Ops <ops@clearstream.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClearStream: immediate support & exec bridge request (today 15:00 PT)

Grace / team,

Thanks for the quick response. We are seeing the exact symptoms you describe — payment authorization timeouts across several EU regions since 02:10 UTC. This is affecting our settlement window and our reconciliation pipeline; we've already had two merchant escalations this morning which will cascade if unresolved by end-of-day.

People joining the bridge: Me (Alex Turner - Head of Platform), Priya Singh (SRE), and Marco Ruiz (Payments Ops).

Acceptable short-term actions: a rollback to v2.3 is fine if that will immediately reduce latency and errors. We also need a firm commitment window for remediation and any commercial concessions for the outage (ClearStream will expect credits for lost throughput / missed SLAs).

We will join at 15:00 PT. Please confirm the conferencing link.

Alex Turner
Head of Platform — ClearStream

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Post-bridge: action items, approvals requested, and commercial path

Team / Leadership,

Quick readout from today's 15:00 PT bridge with ClearStream (participants: Alex Turner, Priya Singh, Marco Ruiz):
- We executed a rollback to model v2.3 as a stopgap at 15:25 PT; observed queue depth reduction within 9 minutes and 95th pct latency fell to ~260ms for the affected routes.
- Root cause: v2.4 increased KV working set causing memory pressure and batch fragmentation; because their reserved pool was at capacity we couldn't autoscale more slots automatically.
- Customer asks: (1) formal credit for the window 02:10–15:25 UTC, (2) a remediation ETA for v2.4 kernel fixes or an optimized quantized build they can run.

Actions we completed:
- Rollback executed and validated (Marissa)
- Temporary shard re-route staged for non-critical jobs (Olga)
- Customer committed to retest v2.4 in a canary lane after we provide tuned kernels (R&D)

Requested approvals (please respond):
1) Approve emergency burst authorization: +20% capacity on rp-clar-3 for up to 6 hours to cover stabilization windows and testing (costed estimate attached in credit_makegood_proposal.pdf).
2) Approve a commercial credit: propose a makegood that covers the outage window; initial draft in attachment. We should offer a partial credit tied to measured token shortfall — sales prefers to avoid open-ended commitments.

If we get approvals for both, Grace will finalize the customer-facing note and legal/finance will prep the credit paperwork (DocuSign link in related_links). R&D lead (cc'ing separately) to prioritize kernel/quant tuning (ETA 48–72 hrs).

Thanks — want to close these items before EOD tomorrow.

Jonas
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Attachments: credit_makegood_proposal.pdf
